body:
@deralmas Thank you for taking the time to review this PR.


> What other issues have you been seeing? Are there issue reports open?

I searched for an existing issue describing exactly the same behavior, but I could not find one.

I think this issue only occurs in a relatively limited configuration: a HiDPI environment using fractional scaling, where the compositor reports logical coordinates or sizes, as is the case with KDE Plasma.

In my testing, GNOME does not exhibit the same issue because the values reported through this code path appear to be effectively equivalent to physical coordinates.

Here is a video showing the problem:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/025a5c30-25f1-4b63-8cbc-a1f07b11ee6d


> Removing "scale compensation" opens a few edge cases. Notably, changing the output scale while a window is open will lead to the same auto-restore issue.

I was able to reproduce this issue, so I updated the implementation to preserve the original scale compensation logic instead of removing it.

The original logic overwrote the stored physical window size with the logical window size. I changed it so that the logical size is stored separately while the window is closed, without overwriting the physical size used internally.


> Inheriting toplevel scale is somewhat fine, although there are really no guarantees that the window scale will actually be the same as the parent.

Yes, to be honest, I do not yet have a complete solution for this part.

For now, I think inheriting the parent window's scale is a reasonable fallback. In the longer term, a more fundamental implementation of per-screen or per-window scaling, such as the work discussed in #86022, would likely be the proper solution.


This PR is not a perfect solution, but it at least brings the popup behavior closer to what Godot currently provides on Windows and macOS.

After this PR, the behavior is as follows:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43b74bdb-a133-456a-be4e-4dd3a4f20318
